en: The Sūtra on the Four Nirayas Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
[In the] Garden.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"There are four great hells."
What are the four? O bhikṣus!
They are the great hell Tiṣya, the great hell Kokālika, the great hell Devadatta, and the great hell Makkhali.
“Monks! In that great hell of Tiṣya, flames twenty cubits long issue from the body; monks!”
In the Gopati Great Hell, the bodies emit flames thirty cubits long; O Bhikṣus!
In the Devadatta Great Hell, the bodies emit flames forty cubits long.
From the body of Makarī, the great hell-being, flames sixty cubits long burst forth.

Should there be any people who, seeking peace and security, desire to obtain their goal by pouring upon that body the waters of thirty great oceans, those ocean waters would be entirely consumed without extinguishing the fire, which would remain like molten copper.
If someone were to place twenty drops of water into that molten copper, those drops would be instantly extinguished; yet it was the same with the bhikṣu Tiṣya—the flames did not go out.

Furthermore, if there is someone who desires to seek peace and security and attain its benefit, and they were to pour upon their body the waters of twenty great oceans, those waters would quickly be exhausted.

Why is this so? Because that foolish bhikṣu Tiṣya obstructed the community of bhikṣus, causing them to go without food for one day; by reason of this, he caused the bhikṣu Tiṣya to enter the Great Hell.

If there is a single bhikṣu who, regarding the bhikṣu Kokālika, desires to bring him peace and cause him to attain his welfare, even if he were to pour upon his body the waters of the thirty great oceans, those ocean waters would quickly be exhausted.
It is like copper melted for two days;
if a person were to place thirty drops of water into that molten copper, they would be entirely consumed without remainder—this case is just like that.

If there were someone who, wishing to bring peace and security to the foolish bhikṣu Kokālika, were to pour upon his body the waters of thirty great oceans, those waters of the great oceans would quickly be exhausted.

Why is this so? That foolish bhikṣu Kokālika slandered the bhikṣus Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana; when his body perished and his life ended, he was reborn in the three evil realms and fell into the Padma Hell.
For this reason, the bhikṣu Kokālika entered the great niraya.

As for that great niraya of Devadatta, even if someone were to pour the waters of the forty great oceans over his body in order to bring him peace and security, those great oceans would quickly be exhausted while that fire would not be extinguished.
It is like molten copper heated by three suns; if someone were to pour forty drops of water into that molten copper, they would be instantly consumed without remainder—this case is just like that.

Devadatta is a foolish person; if someone were to arise with the desire to bring him peace and security, even by pouring upon his body the waters of the forty great oceans, those ocean waters would quickly be exhausted, yet that fire would not be extinguished.

Why is this so? Because the foolish Devadatta sought to harm the Tathāgata, murdered an Arhat bhikṣuṇī, and caused schism within the Saṃgha of bhikṣus; when his body perished and his life ended, he went to the three evil realms and was born in the Avīci Hell. By these causes and conditions, that bhikṣu Devadatta entered the great hell, and flames issued from his body forty cubits in length.

"Monks, regarding that great niraya hell of Makarī, even if someone were to arise with the desire to bring about peace and security for it, and were to pour upon its body the waters of the sixty great oceans, those ocean waters would quickly be exhausted, yet that fire would not be extinguished."

For example, if someone were to pour sixty drops of water into molten copper that has been refined for four days, it would be instantly consumed without remainder; such was the case with that Makkhali.

If there were a person who, desiring to attain peace and security, were to pour the waters of sixty great oceans over their body, those great ocean waters would quickly be exhausted, yet this fire would not be extinguished.
Why is this so? Because this foolish Makkhali taught and led one hundred koṭis of people to practice false views; by reason of this, flames sixty cubits long issued from Makkhali’s body.
"Thus it is, monks! These are the four great hells.
Then, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, the monks rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Sutra on the Four Nirayas Spoken by the Buddha
